title: Lavender Tallow Balm: My Weird Jar of Beef Fat That Actually Works
body:
Okay so I bought beef fat for my face. I know. It sounds like something you’d find in a weird historical reenactment kit, not on your bathroom shelf next to the toothpaste. My first thought was literally just “ew.” But my skin last winter was a disaster. Like, flaky, itchy, angry desert disaster. I’d tried the expensive stuff in the fancy glass bottles, the drugstore lotions that smelled like a chemical factory, the whole nine yards. Nothing stuck. Or it did stick, in a greasy, sit-on-top-of-your-skin kind of way. I was desperate. And scrolling Etsy at like 1 AM in bed, wearing these socks with holes in the heels, and I saw this thing called whipped tallow balm. Lavender. Made in France. I clicked on it mostly as a joke. Beef tallow skincare. Seriously.

But then I read the description. And I got weirdly curious. Here’s the thing.

## How I Ended Up Putting Beef Fat on My Face

It started with my elbows. Random, I know. But they were like sandpaper. I’d scratch them absentmindedly while watching TV and it was just… crusty. Gross. So when this little jar arrived—it’s smaller than you think, fits in your palm—I wasn’t ready to commit my whole face. I opened it. Smelled like lavender maybe? Or not. Something. Herbal. Not like a candle. More like… the plant itself got stuck in there. The texture was weird. Not bad weird. It was solid but soft, like cold butter straight from the fridge. I scooped a tiny bit with my finger. Cold at first. Then it just melted. I rubbed it into one elbow.

I left it on all night. Woke up, totally forgot about it. Showered. Later that day I went to lean on the counter and my elbow slid. It just… slid. No catch. No rough patch. I actually looked at it. The skin was still there, obviously, but it was quiet. Calm. Not healed, but not screaming at me. That was the first “huh” moment. I didn’t expect much but honestly, that got me.

So I started reading. Why beef tallow for skin? It sounds medieval. But the science-y bit, the way it was explained to me (and by “to me” I mean I fell down a Google rabbit hole instead of working), is kinda simple. Our skin makes oil, right? Sebum. Tallow from grass-fed cows is apparently really close to that. Closer than any plant oil or lab-made silicone. So your skin recognizes it. It doesn’t just sit there as a greasy layer; it actually gets absorbed. It’s like giving your skin something it already knows how to use. My grandma would’ve called it common sense. She used lard for everything. Cooking, sure, but also on her hands in winter. She’d just say “it works.” No fancy terms. No “skincare regimen.” Just… it works.

Anyway. After the elbow test, I got brave.

## What This Lavender Tallow Balm Actually Does

I use it at night now. After I wash my face. My routine is basically non-existent, so adding this was a big deal. I scoop a little—a pea size, maybe less—warm it between my fingers, and just pat it on. It feels… I don’t know how to describe it. Not oily. Not like a cream. It’s more like your skin drinks it and then just feels like skin. But better skin. Protected skin. The lavender part is key for me because my brain does not shut off. Ever. The ritual of it, the smell, it’s like a signal. This smell means bed. Means stop. It’s not a strong perfume smell, it’s just this green, quiet, herbal thing. It doesn’t smell like beef. At all. Which, thank god.

I’ve been using it for a few weeks. Maybe a month? I lost track. Time is fake. But my skin is different. The dry patches on my cheeks are gone. Completely. My forehead isn’t a tight drumhead by 10 AM. I used to get these little flaky bits around my nose, especially in spring with the weird weather changes. Gone. It’s not a miracle. I still have pores. I still get a zit if I eat too much pizza. But the baseline? The constant low-level complaint my skin had going on? It’s quiet. It’s just… content. I keep touching my face because it feels normal. Not sticky. Not slick. Just normal. But the good kind of normal. The kind I forgot existed.

Oh, and my hands. I started using the leftovers on my fingers on my hands. Game changer. No more cracks by my knuckles. I wash my hands a million times a day and they used to look wrecked. Now they’re just… hands. It’s wild.

## Would I Buy This Weird Jar Again?

Yeah. I already did. I’m on my second one. The first jar lasted forever, honestly. You need so little. I got mine from this little Etsy shop that makes it in small batches. I like that. Feels less weird than buying a tub of beef fat from a giant corporation. This feels… considered. The ingredients list is short. Grass-fed beef tallow, some lavender oil, that’s basically it. I can pronounce everything. In a world where my moisturizer used to have twenty-five ingredients I needed a chemistry degree to understand, that’s nice. Simple.

I told my sister about it. She has eczema, the real kind, and she was super skeptical. I just gave her my first jar when it was almost empty and said “try it on one patch.” She texted me a week later asking for the link. She said it was the only thing that didn’t burn and actually made the redness go down. That’s not a scientific study. That’s just my sister not being itchy for once.

Look, it’s not for everyone. The idea freaks people out. I get it. It freaked me out. If you’re looking for a pretty-smelling, brightly packaged lotion from a fancy store, this ain’t it. It’s a simple thing. It’s a little jar of whipped fat that smells like a herb garden. But my skin hasn’t been this calm in years. Maybe ever. I don’t know what magic they do in France to make it, but it works. It just does. My skin’s happy. I’m happy. That’s the whole point, right?

Anyway. If your skin is being difficult, feeling tight, itchy, or just generally pissed off at the world, this might be worth a shot. A weird shot, but a shot.

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Weirdly, yeah. Because it’s so similar to the oils our own skin makes, it absorbs deep instead of sitting on top. It’s like giving your skin food it actually knows how to eat. My grandma knew this. Science is just catching up.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
Not in my experience. And I’m prone to clogging. It absorbs clean. It’s not like slathering on cooking grease. The whipped texture is light, and it just sinks in. If you use a tiny amount, you’re golden.

**What does the lavender tallow balm smell like?**
It smells like actual lavender. Not candy lavender. Not soap lavender. It’s green and herbal and a little earthy. It’s calming. It’s the main reason I use it at night—that smell tells my brain it’s time to shut off.
